extracted.intended_audience: general public; researchers, students, and policymakers seeking country/region reference data
extracted.subtask_description: Structured country/region reference profile listing standard geographic, demographic, political, economic, communications, transportation, military, and transnational data fields and short explanatory background notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical and current political overview including major historical events and current issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concise context such as colonization, independence, regime change, ongoing conflicts, economic and political challenges (e.g., Indonesia: Dutch colonization, Japanese occupation, independence negotiations; Iran: 1979 Islamic revolution and aftermath).

rubrics_metrics.name: Location
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of geographic position relative to continents, oceans, and neighboring regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'body of water between Africa, the Southern Ocean, Asia, and Australia' (Indian Ocean); 'Southeastern Asia, archipelago between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific Ocean' (Indonesia); 'Middle East, bordering the Gulf of Oman, the Persian Gulf, and the Caspian Sea' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Latitudinal and longitudinal coordinates used to locate the country/region (given as degrees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '20 00 S, 80 00 E' (Indian Ocean); '5 00 S, 120 00 E' (Indonesia); '32 00 N, 53 00 E' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Map references
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of map or regional mapping references used to place the country/region (e.g., 'Political Map of the World', 'Southeast Asia', 'Middle East').

rubrics_metrics.name: Area
rubrics_metrics.description: Total area with possible breakdown into land and water areas (given in square kilometers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include total area and water/land split (Indonesia: total 1,919,440 sq km; water 93,000 sq km; land 1,826,440 sq km).

rubrics_metrics.name: Area - comparative
rubrics_metrics.description: A comparative statement that relates the country's/region's size to a known entity (e.g., 'about 5.5 times the size of the US', 'slightly less than three times the size of Texas', 'slightly larger than Alaska').

rubrics_metrics.name: Coastline
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of the coastline in kilometers and relevant notes (e.g., inclusion of sea borders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '66,526 km' (Indian Ocean), '54,716 km' (Indonesia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maritime claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Official maritime claims such as territorial sea, exclusive economic zone (EEZ), contiguous zone, continental shelf notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example phrasing: 'territorial sea: 12 nm; exclusive economic zone: 200 nm; measured from claimed archipelagic straight baselines.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal climate regimes and seasonal patterns (monsoons, tropical, arid, etc.) and notable weather phenomena (tropical cyclones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'northeast monsoon (December to April), southwest monsoon (June to October); tropical cyclones occur during May/June and October/November' (Indian Ocean); 'tropical; hot, humid; more moderate in highlands' (Indonesia); 'mostly arid or semiarid, subtropical along Caspian coast' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrain
rubrics_metrics.description: General description of topography, oceanographic or landform features, and major physiographic elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Indian Ocean: 'surface dominated by counterclockwise gyre... ocean floor dominated by Mid-Indian Ocean Ridge'; Indonesia: 'mostly coastal lowlands; larger islands have interior mountains'; Iran: 'rugged, mountainous rim; high, central basin with deserts, mountains; small, discontinuous plains along both coasts.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevation extremes
rubrics_metrics.description: Lowest and highest points with elevations (meters) and name of feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'lowest point: Java Trench -7,258 m; highest point: sea level 0 m' (Indian Ocean); 'highest point: Puncak Jaya 5,030 m' (Indonesia); 'lowest point: Caspian Sea -28 m; highest point: Kuh-e Damavand 5,671 m' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural resources
rubrics_metrics.description: List of major natural resources such as hydrocarbons, minerals, fishery resources, timber, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'oil and gas fields, fish, shrimp, sand and gravel aggregates, placer deposits, polymetallic nodules' (Indian Ocean); 'petroleum, tin, natural gas, nickel, timber, bauxite, copper, fertile soils, coal, gold, silver' (Indonesia); 'petroleum, natural gas, coal, chromium, copper, iron ore, lead, manganese, zinc, sulfur' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal natural hazards affecting the country/region (earthquakes, tsunamis, cyclones, floods, volcanic activity, occasional icebergs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'occasional icebergs pose navigational hazard in southern reaches' (Indian Ocean); 'occasional floods, severe droughts, tsunamis, earthquakes, volcanoes, forest fires' (Indonesia); 'periodic droughts, floods; dust storms, sandstorms; earthquakes' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment - current issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary environmental concerns and threats (pollution, endangered species, deforestation, wetland loss, oil pollution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'endangered marine species include the dugong, seals, turtles, and whales; oil pollution in the Arabian Sea, Persian Gulf, and Red Sea' (Indian Ocean); 'deforestation; water pollution from industrial wastes, sewage; air pollution in urban areas; smoke and haze from forest fires' (Indonesia); 'air pollution... deforestation; overgrazing; desertification; oil pollution in the Persian Gulf; wetland losses from drought.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Geography - note
rubrics_metrics.description: Special geographic or strategic notes such as major chokepoints, archipelagic nature, strategic maritime location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'major chokepoints include Bab el Mandeb, Strait of Hormuz, Strait of Malacca...'; 'archipelago of 17,508 islands (6,000 inhabited); strategic location astride or along major sea lanes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy - overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative summary of the economy, main challenges, structure and policy context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides summary of major economic drivers, structural problems, reform efforts, and key sectors (examples include oil dependence, privatization issues, effects of terrorism, corruption, IMF programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: GDP (and GDP metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross domestic product measures including PPP values, real growth rate, GDP per capita, and composition by sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'purchasing power parity - $758.8 billion (2003 est.)'; 'GDP - real growth rate 4.1% (2003 est.)'; 'GDP - composition by sector: agriculture, industry, services.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment (gross fixed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross fixed investment as percentage of GDP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Investment (gross fixed): 19.7% of GDP (2003)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poverty and income distribution metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Population below poverty line, household income shares, Gini index and related inequality measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Population below poverty line: 27% (1999)'; 'Household income or consumption by percentage share: lowest 10%: 4%; highest 10%: 26.7% (1999)'; 'Gini index: 37 (2001)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflation and fiscal variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer price inflation, budget revenues and expenditures, public debt, current account balance, external debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Inflation rate (consumer prices): 6.6% (2003 est.)'; 'Budget: revenues $40.91 billion; expenditures $44.95 billion (2003 est.)'; 'Public debt: 72.9% of GDP (2003)'; 'Current account balance: $7.336 billion (2003)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Exports and imports totals, principal commodities exported/imported, and major trading partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Exports: $63.89 billion f.o.b. (2003 est.)'; 'Exports - commodities: oil and gas, electrical appliances, plywood, textiles, rubber'; 'Exports - partners: Japan 22.3%, US 12.1%...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and exchange rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Official currency name, currency code, and sample exchange rates against the US dollar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Currency: Indonesian rupiah (IDR)'; 'Exchange rates: Indonesian rupiahs per US dollar - 8,577.13 (2003), 9,311.19 (2002)...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of fiscal year timing or any recent changes to the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Fiscal year: calendar year; note - previously was 1 April - 31 March, but starting with 2001, has been changed to calendar year.'

rubrics_metrics.name: People - population
rubrics_metrics.description: Total population estimate and date of estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Population: 238,452,952 (July 2004 est.)' (Indonesia); 'Population: 69,018,924 (July 2004 est.)' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: People - age structure and median age
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of population by age cohorts and median age for total and by sex where provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '0-14 years: 29.4%; 15-64 years: 65.5%; 65 years and over: 5.1% (2004 est.)'; 'Median age: total: 26.1 years.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Population growth and vital rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Population growth rate, birth rate, death rate, infant mortality, total fertility rate, life expectancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include numeric rates and sex-disaggregated infant mortality and life expectancy where provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health - HIV/AIDS statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Adult prevalence rate, people living with HIV/AIDS, and AIDS-related deaths (if provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'HIV/AIDS - adult prevalence rate: 0.1% (2003 est.); people living with HIV/AIDS: 110,000 (2003 est.)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality / Ethnic groups / Religions / Languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard demographic descriptors including nomenclature for nationals and distributions of ethnic groups, religions, and major languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Nationality: noun Indonesian(s); adjective Indonesian'; 'Ethnic groups: Javanese 45%, Sundanese 14%...'; 'Religions: Muslim 88%...'; 'Languages: Bahasa Indonesia (official), English, Dutch, local dialects...'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Literacy definition used and literacy rates for total and by sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'definition: age 15 and over can read and write; total population: 87.9%; male: 92.5%; female: 83.4% (2002)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government - country name and government type
rubrics_metrics.description: Official long and short forms of the country's name, former names, local long/short forms, and type of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'conventional long form: Republic of Indonesia; conventional short form: Indonesia'; 'Government type: republic' (Indonesia); 'Government type: theocratic republic' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government - capital and administrative divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of the capital and list/description of administrative divisions (provinces, regions, special districts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Capital: Jakarta'; 'Administrative divisions: 30 provinces...'; 'special regions noted (Aceh, Yogyakarta).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Government - independence and constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of independence and constitution information including key dates and notes about amendments or restorations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Independence: 17 August 1945; Netherlands recognizes Indonesian independence 27 December 1949'; 'Constitution: August 1945, abrogated by Federal Constitution of 1949... restored 5 July 1959' (Indonesia example of constitutional history).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal system and suffrage
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of the legal tradition and electorate eligibility/age for voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Legal system: based on Roman-Dutch law, substantially modified by indigenous concepts' (Indonesia); 'Suffrage: 17 years of age; universal' (Indonesia) vs 'Suffrage: 15 years of age; universal' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive branch details
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief of state and head of government, names where provided, election method and dates, and cabinet appointment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lists of current officeholders, election information, notes like 'the president is both the chief of state and head of government'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative branch details
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure of the legislature (unicameral/bicameral), number of seats, term lengths, and recent election dates and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'unicameral House of Representatives or Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat (DPR) (550 seats; members serve five-year terms)'; combined assemblies (people's consultative assembly) and their roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic notes on supreme or constitutional courts and special courts where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Supreme Court or Mahkamah Agung; separate Constitutional Court invested in 2003' (Indonesia); 'Supreme Court - above a special clerical court, a revolutionary court, and a special administrative court' (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: Political parties and pressure groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing of major political parties, leaders, and prominent pressure groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: provides party names and leaders (Indonesia) and lists of pressure groups or pro-reform/opposition groups (Iran).

rubrics_metrics.name: International organization participation
rubrics_metrics.description: List of international organizations the country participates in or to which it is a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long enumerations of bodies such as APEC, ASEAN, UN, IMF, IBRD, WHO, WIPO, WTO, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diplomatic representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on diplomatic representation in and from the US (ambassadors, chancery addresses, consulates, telephone/fax).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include names of chiefs of mission, embassy addresses and contact details, and consulate locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag description
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of national flag including colors, symbols, and comparisons to similar flags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'two equal horizontal bands of red (top) and white; similar to the flag of Monaco' (Indonesia); detailed emblem description for Iran.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications - telephone and broadcast data
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of main telephone lines, mobile cellular subscribers, telephone system assessment, radio and television broadcast stations and device counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Telephones - main lines in use: 7.75 million (2002)'; 'Television broadcast stations: 41 (1999)'; 'Telephone system: domestic service fair, international service good.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications - internet and computing
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet country code, number of internet hosts, ISPs, and internet users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Internet country code: .id'; 'Internet hosts: 62,036 (2003)'; 'Internet users: 8 million (2002)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation - railways, highways, waterways, pipelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Core transport infrastructure metrics such as lengths of railways, total roadways (paved/unpaved), navigable waterways, and pipeline lengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Railways: total: 6,458 km'; 'Highways total: 342,700 km; paved: 158,670 km; unpaved: 184,030 km.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ports and harbors / Merchant marine / Airports
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal ports and harbors, merchant fleet summary, number and characteristics of airports and heliports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides named major ports (e.g., Chennai, Colombo, Durban, Jakarta, Mumbai), merchant marine composition, 'Airports - with paved runways' breakdown by runway length categories, and counts such as 'Airports: 661 (2003 est.)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military - organization and manpower
rubrics_metrics.description: Branches of the armed forces, conscription/compulsory service age and obligation, manpower availability and fit figures, and annual numbers reaching military age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Indonesia Armed Forces (TNI): Army, Navy (including Marines), Air Force'; '18 years of age for compulsory and voluntary military service; conscript service obligation - 2 years (2002)'; 'males age 15-49: 66,458,805 (2004 est.)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Military spending in dollar terms and as percent of GDP (with fiscal year where provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Military expenditures - dollar figure: $1 billion (FY98)'; 'Military expenditures - percent of GDP: 1.3% (FY98)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transnational issues - disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: International and maritime disputes or unresolved boundary claims affecting the country/region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'some maritime disputes (see littoral states)'; Indonesia: East Timor boundary issues, Sipadan and Ligitan, maritime boundary issues with Australia; Iran: strategic location on Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transnational issues - refugees / IDPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and context for refugees and internally displaced persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'IDPs: 535,000 (government offensives against rebels in Aceh; most IDPs in Aceh, Central Kalimantan, Maluku, and Central Sulawesi Provinces) (2004)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transnational issues - illicit drugs
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes on illicit drug production, trafficking, and roles as transshipment points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'illicit producer of cannabis largely for domestic use; possible growing role as transshipment point for Golden Triangle heroin' (Indonesia); 'illicit producer of methaqualone; vulnerable to narcotics money laundering through the hawala system' (earlier regional note).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ports and chokepoints strategic importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of strategically important waterways, canals, straits and chokepoints relevant to commerce and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Four critically important access waterways are the Suez Canal (Egypt), Bab el Mandeb (Djibouti-Yemen), Strait of Hormuz (Iran-Oman), and Strait of Malacca (Indonesia-Malaysia).' (Indian Ocean entry).
